newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-HARRINGTON BREAKS COURSE RECORD IN EUROPEAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HARRINGTON BREAKS COURSE RECORD IN EUROPEAN OPEN.

text.p: Irishman Padraig Harrington broke the course record at the European Open on Thursday a few days after playing some of the most "horrific" golf of his life.
Harrington's seven-under-par 65 at the K Club near Dublin left him a shot clear of Sweden's Niclas Fasth and two ahead of Italian Constantino Rocca.
He hardly played a false shot all day -- a far cry from his performance in the ianaugural World Invitational tournament at Loch Lomond, Scotland, last week.
"I was "hitting some of the worst shots I've ever hit in my life," said Harrington. "I was missing fairways by 100 yards on both sides. Horrific.
"If someone had said I would shoot 65 today I would have laughed. I didn't think it was possible in that wind. I've never come close to breaking 70 here."
Conditions which blew European number one Colin Montgomerie to a 73 and British Open champion Tom Lehman to a 74 failed ruffle Harrington.
Starting with a 25-foot birdie at the 10th, he had another on the short 12th and holed from 40 feet at the 518-yard 18th for an eagle three which earned him two cases of whisky.
On the longer front nine, he added further birdies on the first, second and ninth.
